cells.tense: You are here, past the middle of something, holding the pen.
cells.act: keep the motivation warm with steady care
cells.ask: Set the reason you started this down on a slip of paper and keep it where your eye falls. Read it on the flat days. The finish comes cleaner when the reason for it stays warm — warmth is a small thing tended often rather than a hard push.
cells.core:
You are past the middle of something, still working, and what carries you is that you move from feeling rather than from an outlined plan. Feeling does not hand you the route, but it points the direction, so the next stretch stays lit without being worked out ahead of time. That is why you can be halfway and still know which way forward lies, and why the thing holds together instead of coming apart.
Keep the reason you began warm with steady care. Set it down where you will see it, and read it on the days the work feels like just work. A drive running on feeling wants feeding rather than forcing, and a small reminder read often does more than a hard week. Endings land better when the reason for them is in view.
cells.sheetLine: The ending lands well when the reason you started stays warm.
cells.verb: opening to what you feel before you can name where it leads
cells.place: where what you've lived through gets finished and handed into what's next

cells.tense: You are living past a finish before the last step is taken.
cells.act: tend the small thing and learn from it
cells.ask: Choose one small growing thing you can reach right now, and tend it this week the way a beginner would — watching what it asks for instead of making it move. Turn toward what is still live the care you spend on what is already over.
cells.core:
You are living somewhere past the finish, before the last step is taken — the end already decided, the after already written. Feeling is being spent on what happens once it is over, so the thing on the table now only partly arrives. What is here gets less of you than what is imagined next, and the ending keeps moving further away as a result.
Turn toward something small and tend it as a beginner would, learning what it needs instead of willing it along. Not the whole plan — one growing thing, cared for with hands that do not yet know its ways. Living things keep their own timing, and they teach it by being watched. Care that does not force is what brings you back to where an ending actually happens.
cells.sheetLine: The ending is being lived early, and small live things know better.

cells.place: where what you've lived through gets finished and handed into what's next

cells.tense: You are at a door that closed behind you and have not moved from it.
cells.act: follow a raw curiosity with no use for it
cells.ask: Pick a question you cannot answer and do not need to use. Follow it a little, with no outcome in mind, and see what it turns up before deciding what it is for. No schedule — let it pull when it pulls.
cells.core:
The door behind you is closed, and you have stayed at it, holding what is finished as though it might still need you. Feeling in this stretch is something you look back at rather than move from, so the last ending has not fully landed and the next beginning has not opened. Nothing is pointed forward, and the ground around you belongs to whatever came before.
Let curiosity do the work that pushing cannot. Pick a question you honestly cannot answer and follow it with no use in mind — something you are simply wondering about. Wondering does not wait for you to be motivated or finished first. It lands beside you and goes somewhere, and going somewhere is what shows you a direction is possible from where you are.
cells.sheetLine: A closed door and an honest question can share the same room.
cells.verb: opening to what you feel before you can name where it leads
cells.place: where what you've lived through gets finished and handed into what's next

cells.tense: You are moving by feel through work you would call nothing special.
cells.act: write the facts down in order, without feeling words
cells.ask: Take the thing you would wave off as ordinary and set down what actually happened, in the sequence it happened, with none of the feeling words in the account. Read it back once and hear what it says.
cells.core:
You move by feel through things you would describe as nothing special, and what you have been calling getting through is real work. The sensitivity and fast read you bring are running, and your own account of them keeps them unnamed — so what drives your choices looks like luck or habit, and the strain you have absorbed is filed as ordinary. Nobody watching would know to name it either, because you do not.
Put the account on paper. Set down what actually happened, in its sequence, with none of the feeling words in it. That is a method, not a mood, and it will hold on the days when your sense of things runs loud. A practice you can run without waiting for the right feeling is what keeps the sensitivity working without carrying you off.
cells.sheetLine: What you call nothing special is exactly what the account shows.

attempts.check: The unsupported claim is that the person's feeling-driven direction is genuinely underway and trustworthy right now; a reader could rightly say their inner sense of direction is faint or stalled and has been for a while. The ask still works if I'm wrong about which direction they're in, because finishing and letting go of something small requires no certainty about where they're headed. The sentence that serves me more than them is the one that would congratulate their feeling-led way of moving; the cells instead say plainly what a clean ending looks like in the middle of their life. Note also that the Too Much ask is the partner's own action — tending something small to learn how it grows — never less of the signature.
